creator_or_organization: Founded by Robert Stojnic and Ross Taylor (Atlas ML / Deeptide Ltd). Acquired by Facebook AI (Meta) in December 2019. Sunsetted by Meta in July 2025; successor 'Trending Papers' now maintained by Hugging Face in partnership with Meta.
url: https://paperswithcode.com (now redirects to Hugging Face Trending Papers at https://huggingface.co/papers/trending). Open dataset archive: https://github.com/paperswithcode/paperswithcode-data
content_focus: Papers With Code was the definitive bridge between ML/AI research and practice. Its core mission was connecting published research papers with their code implementations, benchmark results, datasets, and methods. Content was organized around five pillars: (1) Papers linked to official and community code implementations on GitHub; (2) State-of-the-art (SOTA) leaderboards organized as Task/Dataset/Metric tuples, tracking 3,000-5,000+ different tasks with over 1,500 leaderboards; (3) A curated dataset repository with annotated pages featuring sample galleries, statistical summaries, licensing info, and usage notes; (4) A Methods section cataloguing ML techniques (loss functions, activation functions, architectures, etc.); (5) Benchmark tracking showing how models compared across standardized evaluations. The platform expanded beyond ML to cover computer science, physics, mathematics, astronomy, and statistics, ultimately tracking artifacts for over 600,000 research papers. IMPORTANT NOTE: The platform was sunsetted by Meta on July 24-25, 2025, and now redirects to Hugging Face's 'Trending Papers,' which provides paper discovery and code links but lacks the comprehensive SOTA leaderboards and task-level benchmark tracking that defined Papers With Code.
target_audience: Researchers, ML engineers, data scientists, and students. Primarily technical users who need to find code implementations of papers, compare model performance across benchmarks, or discover datasets for specific tasks.
publication_frequency: Continuous (the platform was updated daily with new papers, code links, and benchmark results)
format_and_length: Interactive web platform with searchable database. Users could browse by papers, SOTA benchmarks, datasets, methods, or tasks. Each paper page linked to abstracts, code repositories, benchmark results, and related work. The open dataset behind the platform is available as downloadable JSON files on GitHub under CC-BY-SA license.
accessibility_for_non_engineers: Low. Papers With Code was designed for the research and engineering community. The interface assumed familiarity with ML concepts, benchmark metrics, model architectures, and research paper conventions. Leaderboards compared models using technical metrics (F1 scores, BLEU, perplexity, mAP, etc.) that require domain expertise to interpret. While the platform organized information clearly and was well-designed from a UX perspective, the content itself was deeply technical. For business school students, the platform's main accessible value was understanding which AI tasks are being actively researched and seeing the rapid pace of progress through leaderboard trends, but most content required significant technical background to use meaningfully.
unique_value_proposition: Papers With Code was the only platform that comprehensively linked research papers, code implementations, benchmarks, datasets, and methods in a single unified interface. Its community wiki model allowed anyone to contribute, creating a uniquely comprehensive knowledge graph of ML research. No other platform matched its breadth of SOTA tracking across thousands of tasks. It was the canonical answer to 'what is the current best model for task X?' and 'where is the code for paper Y?' Since its shutdown, no single successor has fully replicated this unified capability: Hugging Face Trending Papers covers paper discovery and code links but has only ~40 tasks vs. 3,000-5,000 on Papers With Code; CodeSOTA focuses on verified benchmarks for specific domains; ORKG preserved some benchmark data but lacks the code-linking functionality.
free_or_paid: Free (fully open access, all data released under CC-BY-SA license)
source_reliability: High. Papers With Code linked directly to published research papers (primarily from arXiv) and official code repositories. Benchmark results were community-curated with links to source papers, enabling verification. The wiki model meant information was crowd-sourced but also crowd-verified. After Meta's acquisition in 2019, the platform had institutional backing and a dedicated team maintaining data quality. The open data license and GitHub archive ensured transparency. Potential limitation: community-reported benchmark results were not independently verified (unlike CodeSOTA's approach), so some leaderboard entries could be inaccurate.
relevance_for_entrepreneurs: Moderate relevance but primarily as a landscape-scanning tool. For AI entrepreneurs, Papers With Code provided a way to quickly assess the state-of-the-art for any given AI task, understand which approaches were gaining traction, and find implementation code to prototype with. The leaderboards helped identify where AI capabilities were mature enough for commercial deployment vs. still research-stage. The datasets section helped find training data for specific use cases. However, the platform was research-oriented and did not directly address business strategy, market sizing, or go-to-market considerations. Since the platform is now shut down, entrepreneurs should use the Hugging Face Trending Papers successor for paper discovery, and consult the archived GitHub dataset for historical benchmark data.
session_mapping: S1 (Fundamentals: understanding the AI research ecosystem and how papers become products), S3 (Projects: finding implementations and benchmarks for specific AI tasks when scoping a project)
last_verified_active: 2026-02-08 (platform sunsetted July 24-25, 2025; paperswithcode.com now redirects to Hugging Face Trending Papers; GitHub data archive remains accessible)
ecosystem_position: Papers With Code occupied a unique and irreplaceable position as the primary aggregator bridging academic ML research and practical implementation. It was the central hub of the research-to-code pipeline: researchers published papers, the community linked implementations, and practitioners used leaderboards to identify best approaches. Its shutdown left a significant gap in the AI information ecosystem. The closest successor is Hugging Face Trending Papers (paper discovery + code links), but the comprehensive benchmark tracking and SOTA leaderboard functionality have not been fully replicated by any single platform. The open dataset on GitHub (CC-BY-SA) preserves the historical data and has spawned community-driven alternatives like PapersWithCodePlus and OpenCodePapers. The ORKG (Open Research Knowledge Graph) at TIB imported Papers With Code benchmark data in 2021, preserving some of the leaderboard knowledge.
